goal: Implements BIP 54 (Consensus Cleanup) validation rules, activated only on regtest for now, leaving mainnet activation for later.
Fixes several long-standing consensus/policy defects: timewarp and Murch-Zawy timestamp exploits, unbounded legacy sigops in a tx, and 64-byte transactions colliding with Merkle-tree inner nodes.
reviewability: Ready. Author has actively addressed review comments and rebased repeatedly, most recently 2026-09-13, with no open material requests.
agreement: Strong concept support from seven reviewers with no objections (dergoegge, fanquake, polespinasa, theStack, hsjoberg, fjahr, stickies-v).
Several detailed technical questions raised (ariard, polespinasa, l0rinc) have been answered or resolved by the author without pushback.

categories.name: validation
why: P1 because it changes what blocks and transactions the node accepts, which is the highest-stakes category of change, even though it is gated behind a regtest-only deployment for now.
It resolves a known set of consensus vulnerabilities (timewarp, Murch-Zawy, sigops DoS, 64-byte tx ambiguity) and forces the project toward a decision on activating Consensus Cleanup.

categories.name: mempool
why: P2 because it moves the BIP54 sigops limit from a bypassable standardness check to a hard consensus rule, closing an `-acceptnonstdtxs` bypass and a marginal-cost DoS vector discussed at length by ariard.
This tightens policy defenses that second-layer protocols and node operators rely on.

categories.name: mining
why: P3 because the mining-relevant Murch-Zawy enforcement already landed separately in #35949, leaving only a constant rename and comment update here.
Low incremental leverage for miners since the substantive template-safety work is already merged elsewhere.

categories.name: rpc
why: P3 because it only adds a new softfork entry to getdeploymentinfo, giving visibility into the new BIP54 deployment status.
Small, low-risk addition with no reported external consumer need.

categories.name: docs
why: P4 because it adds a single line to bips.md documenting BIP 54 support, which is useful but minor relative to the scope of the change.

result.summary: This PR implements the validation rules of BIP 54 (Consensus Cleanup), enabling them only on regtest while leaving mainnet activation for a separate decision. It carries over consensus-critical code previously reviewed and tested on Bitcoin Inquisition: a 2-hour timewarp grace period, the Murch-Zawy negative-interval fix, a hard cap on legacy sigops per transaction, and rejection of 64-byte transactions. The bulk of the diff (~95%) is new unit, functional, and fuzz test coverage including BIP-defined test vectors.
result.problem: Bitcoin Core currently has no way to fix several known consensus-level defects (timewarp and Murch-Zawy timestamp manipulation, unbounded legacy sigops cost, 64-byte transaction/Merkle-tree ambiguity) without a soft fork; this PR provides the implementation so the project can review it and decide on activation, benefiting the network's long-term security and giving developers a concrete artifact to evaluate.

open_concerns: ariard raised a subtle DoS-cost asymmetry in CHECKMULTISIG sigops accounting versus vbyte cost; discussed at length but not resolved as a code change, treated as inherent to reusing BIP16 accounting.

polespinasa noted the new sigops failure is tagged TX_CONSENSUS even though it is a policy-origin check pre-activation; author explained the rationale (avoiding divergence from Inquisition-tested code) rather than changing it.
resolved_concerns: ariard's suggestion to rename 'legacy' terminology in consensus.h was implemented by the author.
fjahr's suggestion to enforce the Murch-Zawy rule in the miner was split out and merged separately as #35949, then this PR rebased on top of it.
l0rinc's question about BIP text using mainnet-specific difficulty-period constants was resolved by author explaining local test network values don't belong in the BIP.
polespinasa's nit on has_value()/value() style was declined by the author with rationale and the reviewer did not push back.

categories.name: validation
categories.evidence: Implements new consensus rules (timewarp grace period, Murch-Zawy fix, sigops limit, 64-byte tx rejection) directly in validation.cpp, consensus/tx_verify.cpp, and consensus/consensus.h, gated by a new versionbits deployment.
categories.rationale: The commit messages describe fixing timewarp and Murch-Zawy timestamp exploits and a sigops-based DoS vector previously discussed on the mailing list by ariard; per the validation rubric, proposed soft forks are P1 because reaching a decision and ensuring correctness if activated matters regardless of activation timing.

uncertainties: Whether the mempool category should be scored higher given the DoS-relevant sigops accounting concern ariard raised remains partly unresolved technically, though not blocking.
Impact of this PR outside validation is modest since most other areas only see mechanical follow-on changes to stay compatible with the new consensus rules.
No explicit maintainer decision yet on eventual mainnet activation, so P1 here reflects the decision-and-correctness framing from the rubric rather than activation urgency.
result.card: This PR implements the full validation logic for BIP 54 (Consensus Cleanup), activated only on regtest, fixing timewarp and Murch-Zawy timestamp exploits, an unbounded legacy-sigops DoS vector, and a 64-byte transaction/Merkle-tree ambiguity, while leaving mainnet activation as a separate future decision. It is based on code already reviewed and tested on Bitcoin Inquisition, with ~95% of the diff being new unit, functional, and fuzz tests including official BIP54 test vectors. Seven reviewers (dergoegge, fanquake, polespinasa, theStack, hsjoberg, fjahr, stickies-v) gave Concept ACK with no objections, and detailed technical concerns from ariard and polespinasa were engaged and resolved or accepted as tradeoffs. The author has stayed active through five rebases, most recently addressing all outstanding comments on 2026-09-13, leaving the PR in a ready-to-review state. A related miner-side fix for the Murch-Zawy rule was split out and merged separately as #35949, and this PR rebased on top of it.
